summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease on home hemodialysis, a mechanical aortic valve, and extensive cardiovascular disease was admitted for chest pain and anemia. She had a troponin elevation consistent with a Type II NSTEMI, exacerbated by severe anemia and hypertension. Due to her complex anatomy, further revascularization was not feasible, so she was managed medically with blood transfusions, optimization of anticoagulation, and addition of isosorbide dinitrate and ranolazine for angina control. Her potassium normalized, and she remained stable throughout the hospitalization. She requested palliative care and expressed her wish to discontinue dialysis after her son’s visit. A MOLST form was completed, and she was discharged home on hospice care with a focus on symptom management and comfort.
